line: Barbara came to stay the week after. She watched me work through my morning routine. I stood in line for ten minutes without shifting my weight.
prompt: INGREDIENTS. @image1 is Her: face, age, hair and build only. These references set what things ARE; the prose below sets what HAPPENS, and nothing in them is a shot to cut to. A plain medium close-up of Her, a woman of seventy-one, standing against the living room of her own house, a plain magnolia wall, soft daylight from the left, the camera on a locked tripod, nothing else in frame. Her looks just off the lens at someone beside the camera and, starting straight away, says these sentences one after another, clearly and completely, with only an ordinary breath between them: "Barbara came to stay the week after. She watched me work through my morning routine. I stood in line for ten minutes without shifting my weight." She keeps speaking from the first second to the last; no long silences. Delivery: An English woman of seventy-one from the north of England, Lancashire, a light, dry, slightly reedy voice with a little gravel at the bottom of her range. Plain northern vowels, flat "a", unhurried and understated — she says the big things quietly and lets a line land without pushing it. A dry humour just under the surface. Statements fall at the end; never sing-song, never theatrical. Level, even and unhurried; conversational volume; no emotion coloured into the words; a person reading a sentence aloud to themselves. Audio is clean production sound from a boom microphone just out of frame above the speaker: close, clear and even, with a little of the room's natural tone behind the voice. Breath and mouth detail are present but never exaggerated. No phone-microphone proximity, no compression pumping, no music and no sound effects anywhere in the clip — dialogue only. The microphone and all equipment stay outside the picture. Dialogue only: no music, no score, no sound effects, no foley, no background ambience events, no singing, no humming, no background music, no soundtrack. One speaker only. NEGATIVES: no other people, no second voice, no microphone in frame, no looking into the lens, no text, no captions, no long pauses, no silent beats, no music, no score, no sound effects, no foley, no background ambience events, no singing, no humming, no background music, no soundtrack.
